business_summary.text: P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited is a Pune-based jewellery retailer operating under the PNG brand, with subsidiaries Gadgil Diamonds Private Limited (India) and PNG Jewelers, Inc. (USA).

call_points.text: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 7% for the full year.
FY27 PAT margin targeted at 4.1-4.25%, excluding hedging gains.
PAT margin targeted at 4.5-4.7% by FY29.
Around 25 stores to be added in FY27, taking the network to about 103 stores.
37 stores planned in each of the next two years, reaching about 177 stores by March 2029.
By March 2029, about 113 stores would be legacy PNG and around 64 Litestyle.
Adjusted gross margin rose 40-50 bps YoY once hedging gains are stripped out.
Borrowings including gold metal loans are about ₹1,500-1,550 Cr, flat versus March.
Hedging to rise to 80% by Q3 and 90-100% next year.
Retail studded ratio improved to 10.9% from 9.9% in the previous quarter.
Franchise revenue growth was muted at 8% on timing of stock payments; management expects it to pick up in Q2 and Q3.
Analysts pressed on flat gross margin despite a better retail mix; management pointed to hedging gains on a larger base and new territories at only about 3% of retail mix.
Management may revise FY27 guidance next quarter depending on how the market situation evolves.
Q4 volume growth was 27% in gold, 37% in silver and 125% in diamond.
QIP remains at an enabling board resolution valid to end-August; management says the business is self-sufficient without it.
An analyst pressed that festive discounts and franchise mix look structural; management said full-year margins absorb them and bullion was the main driver.
Management declined to quantify FY27 volume growth, citing uncertainty a week after the import duty hike.

guidance.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹13,500 Cr with EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%
Inventory hedging to rise to 75-80% in FY27 from 67% at end-FY26
FY27 store openings of 25: 5 COCO and 20 franchise
Gold bars and coins share expected to fall back to around 25% in FY27 from 40% in Q4FY26
FY27 PAT margin of 4.1-4.25% excluding hedging gains
Around 25 stores to be opened in FY27, taking the network to about 103 stores
37 stores to be added in each of the next two years, reaching about 177 stores by March 2029
FY27 other expenses of about ₹400 Cr, roughly 3% of sales
Borrowings to fall below ₹1,000 Cr by FY29 and be debt-free in four to five years
Hedging to reach 80% by Q3 and 90-100% next year

former_names: P N Gadgil Jewellers Pvt. Ltd.

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Durables > Gems, Jewellery And Watches

operating_notes.text: Gold segment continues to be the primary revenue driver
IPO proceeds of ₹8,500 million fully utilised, including ₹3,925.68 million for 12 new Maharashtra stores.
Q4FY26 other expenses rose 156.9% YoY to ₹167.16 Cr, outpacing revenue growth of 123.2%.
Total store count reached 78 stores across 37 cities as of March 31, 2026.
Gold bars and coins were 40% of Q4FY26 revenue (₹1,400 Cr) versus 28% (₹450 Cr) in Q4FY25, and about 32% for FY26.
Bullion gross margin is 0.5-1% versus 12.5-13% on plain gold jewellery and 2.5-3% on franchise sales.
Old gold exchange is around 40% of the business, with make-to-order at 30-35% of sales in Maharashtra and 22% outside it.
Q1FY27 retail studded ratio 10.9% (from 9.9% in Q4FY26); Litestyle stud ratio 32.9%; new North and Central India stores at 15-18%.
53% of gold bars and coins purchases converted into jewellery in Q1FY27, up from 46% a year earlier.
Store count at quarter-end was 78 (57 COCO and 21 FOCO).
Postal ballot closed October 21, 2026 approving PNG ESOP 2026 for company and subsidiary employees, and re-appointment of Independent Director Dr. Vaijayanti Pandit.

holders.name: TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED

segment_mix.segment: Bullion (bars and coins, share of retail revenue)

timeline.summary: PNGJL reported ₹251 Cr revenue on Akshaya Tritiya, 80.3% YoY growth
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,544.31 Cr (+123.2% YoY), net profit ₹90.26 Cr (+45.6% YoY).
P N Gadgil Jewellers reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹3,544.31 Cr, crossing ₹10,000 Cr in revenue for FY26.
Prakhar Gupta signed the conference call audio recording link for Q4 FY26 results discussion on May 15, 2026.
On its Q4FY26 call, P N Gadgil Jewellers held FY27 guidance at ₹13,500 Cr revenue with 7-7.5% EBITDA margin, after Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% gold bars and coins mix.
Q1FY27 call (28 July 2026): revenue ₹2,413 Cr (+41% YoY), EBITDA ₹192.4 Cr at 8% margin, PAT ₹105.3 Cr (+52%); FY27 target of ~103 stores and about 7% EBITDA margin reiterated.
On 14 October 2026, P N Gadgil Jewellers announced that CRISIL reaffirmed its Crisil A+/Stable rating while enhancing total bank loan facilities to ₹600 Cr.
P N Gadgil Jewellers shareholders approved PNG ESOP 2026 via postal ballot despite institutional dissent.

status_history.evidence: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin of 8%, above the ≥5% target.
Borrowings including GML of ₹1,500-1,550 Cr are roughly flat versus March; no finance cost figure given on the call.

watchlist.text: Gold bars and coins share of revenue

watchlist.response: Said full-year margins already absorb these, the discounts were one-time events worth about half a percent, and the main driver was bars and coins at 40% of Q4 sales
watchlist.text: Analyst argued the Q4 margin drag from festive discounts, new-market discounts and rising franchise share looks structural rather than one-off

watchlist.response: Declined to quantify, saying it is difficult a week after the import duty hike; pointed to margin guidance instead
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for FY27 volume growth outlook

watchlist.response: Gave an average of about 60% for the full year after initially repeating quarterly figures
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the full-year FY26 hedging proportion rather than the Q4 figure

watchlist.response: Adjusted gross margin rose 40-50 bps once hedging gains are removed; new territories are only about 3% of retail mix.
watchlist.text: Gross margin flat YoY despite a better retail mix

watchlist.response: Timing of franchise stock payments; expects franchise to pick up in Q2 and Q3.
Enabling board resolution in place; will consider a QIP at a suitable time.
